title: Step cards for 'brushing teeth'
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming sequences and online safety
source: Seeded from computing/y3 lesson 1 (Step cards for 'brushing teeth' (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 1: Algorithms: precise steps and spotting mistakes. To understand that an algorithm is a set of precise steps in the right order

blocks.title: Sort into: 1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th
blocks.answer: 1st: Pick up the toothbrush. 2nd: Put toothpaste on the brush. 3rd: Brush every tooth. 4th: Rinse the brush

questions.q: Write the steps to move from A1 to A4 on the grid.
questions.model: Count the squares between A1 and A4: there are 3 moves. Step: forward 3 squares. Test it with your finger.

questions.q: Spot the bug: to reach B2 from A1 Sam wrote 'forward 1, turn left, forward 1'. What is wrong?
questions.a: He should turn right, not left (facing up, B is to the right).

questions.q: Put in order: 'eat', 'wash hands', 'say Bismillah', 'sit down'.
questions.a: Wash hands, sit down, say Bismillah, eat.

questions.q: Core: On your paper grid, write an algorithm to move the counter from A1 to D4. Number each step.
questions.a: For example: forward 3, turn right, forward 3.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two steps aloud: '1. Forward 3 squares. 2. Turn right.' and checks with a finger on the grid.

questions.q: Extend: Write an algorithm for a grown-up at home to make a cup of water, in at least 5 steps.
questions.a: For example: take a cup, go to the tap, turn the tap on, fill the cup, turn the tap off.

questions.q: Stretch: Write an algorithm with one bug in it. Swap with the screen: can the class find the bug?
questions.a: Any algorithm with one deliberate error, and the fix explained.

questions.q: An algorithm is... A) a computer B) a set of steps in order C) a game
questions.a: B) a set of steps in order
options: A set of steps in order

questions.q: Why must an algorithm be precise?
questions.a: So it can only be followed one way and gives the right result.
